disclaimer: Original study guide keyed to public curriculum; course content itself lives at the source.

checkpoints: Explain why `ls *` in a 300k-file directory fails but `find . -name '*.log'` works
Produce an awk one-liner that sums the 5th column of a CSV and prints the total
Predict the exit code of `false | true` and how to capture the left side's failure
keyConcepts: FHS directory layout (/, /etc, /var, /usr, /opt, /srv)
Globbing vs regex: *, ?, [], brace expansion
Redirection operators (>, >>, <, <<, 2>, &>) and pipe semantics
Exit status propagation and PIPESTATUS
grep -E/P, sed -n s///, awk field processing with FS/OFS
labs: Reconstruct a destroyed directory tree from a find/printf inventory using only coreutils
Write a one-liner pipeline that parses auth logs for top 10 offending IPs and emits a report
Rename 200 files with parameter expansion plus a sed-based bulk rename, verifying before/after with diff
Use tar, gzip, and rsync to build a timestamped incremental backup rotation in ~/backups
objectives: Navigate and manipulate the filesystem efficiently from a bare shell
Compose pipelines using globbing, redirection, pipes, and filters
Extract and transform text with grep, sed, awk, cut, sort, uniq, and xargs
modules.title: CLI Fluency and Text Processing

checkpoints: Which fstab field controls boot behavior if the device is missing, and why does it matter?
Explain a scenario where df shows 40% free yet writes fail
Compare mkfs.ext4 -i vs default inode ratio and when you would tune it
keyConcepts: Partitioning with parted/gdisk; GPT vs MBR tradeoffs
ext4 vs XFS: journaling, online growth, inode allocation
mount options (noatime, ro, nodev, nosuid, discard) and fstab fields
df vs du semantics; inode exhaustion vs block exhaustion
fsck/xfs_repair workflow and when never to run them mounted
labs: On a loop device or cloud VM, partition a disk, format ext4 and XFS, mount with options, and persist via fstab
Fill a filesystem with small files until inode exhaustion, diagnose it, then fix it
Simulate a corrupt journal scenario safely and walk the fsck recovery sequence
Move a directory tree across filesystems preserving ownership, xattrs, and hardlinks with rsync -aHAX
objectives: Partition a disk and create filesystems with the appropriate type for the workload
Mount filesystems with correct options and make mounts persistent via fstab
Inspect and reason about disk usage, inodes, and filesystem health
modules.title: Filesystems, Partitions, and Storage Basics

checkpoints: What mode results from umask 027 on a new directory, and show the arithmetic
Why does setfacl -m u:carol:rw file sometimes grant less than expected?
Predict what happens when you hard-link a file across two mounts
keyConcepts: rwx meaning differs on files vs directories (x = traversal)
umask 022 vs 027: subtractive semantics on file 666/dir 777 bases
setuid/setgid/sticky: where they live and what each enables
ACLs: getfacl/setfacl, mask entries, default ACL inheritance on directories
Hard links (inode sharing) vs symlinks (path indirection); link count behavior on delete
labs: Build a shared project directory with setgid so new files inherit the group, plus a default ACL for two users
Create a file with mode 4755 and demonstrate what setuid actually does vs what people think it does
Lock down an SSH authorized_keys setup: diagnose and fix permission failures step by step
Trace every permission decision for one failing `cat` on a deeply nested path and document the denial point
objectives: Apply chmod/chown/chgrp with symbolic and octal modes confidently
Predict a process's effective access from owner/group/other, umask, and setuid/setgid/sticky bits
Manage fine-grained access with ACLs and reason about hard vs symbolic links
modules.title: Permissions, Ownership, and Access Control

checkpoints: Why is piping curl to apt-key add (deprecated) dangerous, and what replaces it?
Distinguish hold, pin, and exclude; give one use case each
Explain what `dnf provides /usr/bin/foo` queries versus `dnf list installed`
keyConcepts: dpkg vs apt vs aptitude layering; rpm vs dnf layering
Repository metadata, GPG signing, and sources.list / .repo formats
apt pinning (preferences) and dnf module streams / excludes
Version locking, holds, and downgrade semantics
Recovery from dpkg interruptions and rpm database corruption
labs: Add a third-party repo with its GPG key the correct modern way (keyring dir, signed-by), then install from it
Pin a package to a specific version on apt and to a stream on dnf; verify with policy/info
Simulate a broken dpkg state and recover with dpkg --configure -a; simulate an rpm db issue
Build a local offline repo mirror (apt-ftw/create-repo) and install from it on a second VM
objectives: Install, query, and remove software on both apt and dnf families
Configure repositories, keys, and pinning/preferences safely
Troubleshoot broken dependency states and locked package databases
modules.title: Package Management and Repositories

checkpoints: Why does Type=simple with a daemonizing program break Restart= handling?
Translate `0 2 * * *` cron into an OnCalendar expression and note one semantic difference
Explain the difference between `systemctl reload` and `restart` for a running nginx-style service
keyConcepts: Unit types and dependency directives: Wants/Requires, Before/After, PartOf
Type=simple vs forking vs notify; ExecStart/ExecReload/ExecStop semantics
Environment, WorkingDirectory, User/Group, sandboxing directives (ProtectSystem, PrivateTmp)
timer OnCalendar/OnBootSec/OnUnitActiveSec; Persistent=true semantics
journalctl filtering by unit, boot, priority; persistent vs volatile storage
labs: Write a forking-to-simple service unit for a Python app; add hardening directives until systemd-analyze security improves
Replace a cron job with a systemd timer with Persistent=true; verify catch-up after a missed window
Diagnose a deliberately broken service (bad ExecStart path, missing env) using only systemctl status/journalctl
Create a socket-activated service and demonstrate on-demand startup with ss showing the listener
objectives: Author unit files for services, timers, sockets, and targets
Control service lifecycle and diagnose failures from unit state and logs
Use timers as cron replacements with calendar and monotonic triggers
modules.title: systemd: Units, Services, Timers, and the Journal

checkpoints: A host pings its gateway but nothing beyond: list three distinct causes and how to test each
Why does allowing ESTABLISHED,RELATED matter in a default-deny INPUT chain?
Explain the security value and limits of moving SSH off port 22
keyConcepts: ip addr/route/link; ss vs netstat; nmcli/networkd vs static config
CIDR, longest-prefix match, default route, source address selection
DNS resolution path: /etc/resolv.conf, nsswitch, systemd-resolved stubs
iptables/nftables chains and tables; default-deny posture, stateful ESTABLISHED,RELATED
sshd_config hardening: key-only auth, root login, AllowUsers, nonstandard port tradeoffs, fail2ban basics
labs: Bring up a second interface with a static /24, add a route, and prove asymmetric routing works with ping -I
Break DNS three different ways (resolv.conf, nsswitch, upstream) and diagnose each with getent/drill/dig
Write an nftables/iptables ruleset: default deny in, allow 22/80/443 + established, log-and-drop the rest
Harden sshd (key-only, no root, AllowUsers), verify with a second terminal, then set up key-based login properly
objectives: Configure addresses, routes, and interfaces with the iproute2 toolkit
Diagnose connectivity layer by layer: link, local, gateway, DNS, remote
Implement host firewall rules and lock down SSH to a sane posture
modules.title: Networking: ip, Routing, DNS, Firewall, SSH

checkpoints: What does `sudo -l` reveal that `id` does not?
Explain why editing /etc/sudoers directly is dangerous and what visudo buys you
Distinguish a locked account (passwd -l) from an expired one (chage -E) in auth behavior
keyConcepts: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group field semantics; UID/GID allocation
sudoers syntax, visudo, Cmnd_Alias, NOPASSWD risks, sudo -l auditing
PAM stack basics: auth/account/password/session; pam_faillock, pam_pwquality
chage password aging; locked vs expired vs nologin accounts
SELinux/AppArmor modes awareness; auditd watch rules for sensitive files
labs: Create a deploy user with restricted sudo: only systemctl restart of two services; prove broader commands are denied
Enforce password quality and lockout policy via PAM on a test VM; trigger and clear a faillock
Audit a machine: find world-writable files, SUID binaries, and accounts with empty/expired passwords
Set up auditd watches on /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow and review the resulting log entries
objectives: Provision users/groups with correct defaults, shells, and home skeleton
Delegate privilege with least-privilege sudoers rules and validate them
Apply a baseline hardening pass: PAM basics, password policy, audit trail
modules.title: Users, Groups, sudo, and Security Posture

checkpoints: Why does `set -e` not save you inside `if` conditions or `cmd || fallback`?
Explain what `trap 'rm -f $tmp' EXIT` guarantees that manual cleanup does not
Two cron jobs overlap and corrupt output: name two mechanisms that prevent this
keyConcepts: set -euo pipefail and where it still bites; quoting "$@" vs $*
Exit codes: 0-255, 127/126 meanings, capturing vs masking in pipelines
trap on EXIT/ERR/INT for cleanup; mktemp for temp files; flock for mutual exclusion
Functions, getopts, here-docs; idempotency as a design goal
cron environment minimalism (PATH), MAILTO, and overlap protection
labs: Write a backup script that is idempotent, locks with flock, logs to syslog, and exits nonzero with context on failure
Refactor a fragile script: add set -u quoting fixes until shellcheck passes clean
Schedule a cron job that previously failed from environment issues; fix PATH and prove it runs unattended
Build a health-check script emitting Nagios-style exit codes consumed by a monitoring probe
objectives: Write robust bash scripts with error handling, quoting, and argument parsing
Use exit codes, traps, and logging so scripts fail loudly and safely
Schedule and supervise recurring work with cron and systemd timers
modules.title: Shell Scripting and Automation

checkpoints: Your VM drops to emergency shell at boot: what are your first three commands and why?
A service shows active (running) but clients time out: what do you check before blaming the app?
Explain how to prove an OOM kill versus a segfault from logs alone
keyConcepts: The layers: hardware -> bootloader -> kernel -> init -> services -> app; bisect at layer boundaries
GRUB rescue, initramfs shell, systemd rescue/emergency targets, chroot from live media
dmesg/journal -b for boot faults; blkid/fstab mismatches as classic no-boot cause
iostat/vmstat/free/sar for resource pressure; distinguishing OOM from leaks
tcpdump and ss state inspection for 'service up but unreachable' cases
labs: Break fstab with a wrong UUID, reboot to emergency target, and recover (do this in a VM snapshot)
Kill a service's dependency and trace the failure from journal through unit state to the root config line
Diagnose a disk-full scenario where df disagrees with du (deleted-but-open files) and fix it live
Debug a black-hole network path: traceroute + tcpdump to find the silent drop point
objectives: Apply a repeatable isolate-and-verify method to any outage
Recover a system that fails to boot: GRUB, initramfs, fstab, rescue targets
Triangulate disk, memory, and network faults with the right first command
modules.title: Troubleshooting Methodology: Boot, Services, Disk, Network
